entries.label: EMA News
entries.title: Global regulators call for advancing alternatives to animal testing across the medicine lifecycle

entries.summary: EMA has endorsed a joint statement urging the advancement of alternatives to animal testing throughout the medicine lifecycle.
entries.why_it_matters: The statement signals a shift toward non‑animal testing approaches, prompting RA teams across all therapeutic areas to review and update their development plans and documentation accordingly.

entries.why_it_matters: RA teams should identify the appropriate national contact point to coordinate compliance and reporting related to QR code implementation for veterinary products.

entries.label: EMA Guidelines
entries.title: Substances considered as not falling within the scope of Regulation (EC) No. 470/2009, with regard to residues of veterinary medicinal products in foodstuffs of animal origin
entries.description: Substances considered as not falling within the scope of Regulation (EC) No. 470/2009, with regard to residues of veterinary medicinal products in foodstuffs of animal origin
entries.summary: Certain substances are now excluded from the scope of Regulation (EC) No. 470/2009 regarding residues of veterinary medicinal products in foodstuffs of animal origin.
entries.why_it_matters: RA teams must recognize that these excluded substances will no longer be subject to the same residue monitoring and reporting requirements under the regulation.
